sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bonded Warehouse Wholesale Trade of Aged Scotch and Bordeaux Wines

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU Treaties (TFEU and EU CETA as EU-Singapore FTA by extension)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 et seq. and L561-10-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 12 février 2020; Décret n° 2020-974 du 5 août 2020; Code de commerce, Article L225-102-4 (register of beneficial owners held by the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés); Regulation (EU) 2018/1673 on money laundering countermeasures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Rédigés par notaire or legal counsel, filed with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Attestation de domiciliation du siège social (Registered Office Domiciliation Agreement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Domiciliation company or physical office lessor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if foreign lessor, otherwise domestic notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for foreign UBO identity documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identité et domicile des dirigeants (Identity and Residence Proof of Directors)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authorities and local municipality or foreign consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign public documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Rapport du commissaire aux apports (Capital Contribution Auditor's Report)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification / Apostille if used abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory systematic screening of all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated Lists, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, French national asset-freeze list (Décisions de gel des avoirs), and French Financial Intelligence Unit (Tracfin) guidelines. Enhanced due diligence is statutorily required for politically exposed persons (PEPs) under Articles L561-10 and L561-10-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, including beneficial owner identification, source of funds checks, and continuous transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (INPI) / Infogreffe / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All legal texts must be drafted in French. A company name may include foreign words but must be written using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin scripts must be phonetically transliterated. The name must be lawful, not contrary to public order, and must not infringe existing trademarks or create confusion with prior companies. The name must include or be preceded by the legal form indicator 'SAS'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the Registrar (Greffier du Tribunal de Commerce) or an objection raised by INPI, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration request (recours gracieux) with the rejecting authority within two months. If the rejection is confirmed or not withdrawn, a judicial appeal must be filed before the Tribunal de Commerce within fifteen days of the refusal decision. Where the rejection is grounded in a trademark conflict, the applicant may also initiate an invalidation or opposition action before the INPI within two months of publication. The reservation window may be renewed by filing a fresh name search before the expiration of the initial 30-day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permitted for a SAS under the requirements of Law n° 2005-882 of 2 August 2005, provided the domiciliation service provider offers a physical reception facility, meeting room, and guaranteed mail handling. However, for bonded warehouse wholesale trade in wine and spirits, a purely nominal virtual office will not satisfy substantive commercial or customs conditions. The French Customs and Indirect Taxation Authority (Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects) requires a licenced physical bonded warehouse or contractual access to one, along with adequate storage and traceability infrastructure. Therefore, a physical operational address is mandatory for licensing approval even if a virtual office is accepted for postal residency.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (75% probability within the first 12 months). Bonded warehouse licensees engaged in wholesale wine and spirits are subject to routine and unannounced physical inspections by French Customs (DGDDI) under the Union Customs Code and the French Code général des impôts. Stock reconciliation, physical inventory verification, seal integrity checks, and tax due diligence audits are conducted at the bonded warehouse and the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and availability verification before the INPI/RCS database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Infogreffe (official fee may be waived for direct search, attorney bench fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate legal verification in France

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO and AML due diligence package (screening of shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners against sanctions/PEP lists)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance service provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for KYC/AML professionals and market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of French SAS Articles of Association (Statuts) and legal advice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate formation legal counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement (first annual fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation company or physical office provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for corporate postal and registered office services in France

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Appointment and fees of the commissaire aux comptes if capital contributions in kind are used (voluntary or mandatory threshold)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Legal tariff and professional fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing fees for incorporation with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and publication of legal notice (Annonce légale)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffes du Tribunal de Commerce / legal journal publisher
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff for corporate registry and mandatory legal advertisement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary customs and bonded warehouse licence consultation (DGDDI requirements)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Customs broker or specialized trade lawyer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for French customs regulatory advice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (SAS), and Articles R.123-1 et seq. (registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and M0 form (Déclaration de création d'une personne morale)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS; however, capital must be fully subscribed and paid up to at least 50% of the nominal value upon incorporation, with the remainder paid within 5 years. No escrow account required unless capital is contributed in kind, which requires a statutory auditor's report (commissaire aux apports).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the company is duly incorporated under the French Commercial Code as a Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS). The shareholders hereby subscribe to the share capital as set forth in the Articles of Association. The registered office is fixed at [address], France. The undersigned appoint [Name] as President, [Name] as General Manager, and [Name] as Statutory Auditor (if applicable). The President is authorized to complete all formalities with the RCS, publish the legal notice, and open a corporate bank account. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private notary (notaire) or online legal platform; notarization required if real estate contribution or if shareholders opt for notarial form
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, including corporate name, registered office, share capital, share classes, governance rules, and object clause covering bonded warehouse wholesale trade of wines and spirits. If capital includes non-cash contributions, obtain a commissaire aux apports report. Sign by all shareholders (or their proxies). Notarize if required.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office (lease or ownership deed)
Commissaire aux apports report (if non-cash contributions)
Bank certificate of capital deposit (if cash contributions)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the Statuts, correct the identified clauses and resubmit. If notarization is missing, arrange notarial execution within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notice in a Journal of Legal Notices (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any authorized legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a notice containing the corporate name, legal form (SAS), capital, registered office, object, and duration. Publish in a JAL approved for the department. Obtain a certificate of publication (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected, correct the content and republish. Ensure the JAL is authorized for the department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with RCS (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed M0 form, signed Statuts, legal notice certificate, proof of capital deposit, and identification documents. Pay the filing fee. The registry will issue a K-bis extract (official certificate of incorporation) upon approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is incomplete, the registry issues a query (demande de régularisation). Respond within 30 days with the missing documents. If rejected, correct and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax and Social Security (SIREN/SIRET, VAT, and Employer Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE (Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques) and URSSAF (social security)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the company automatically receives a SIREN number. VAT registration is automatic for EU entities. For employer registration, file with URSSAF to obtain a social security number. This is often done via the formalities portal (guichet-entreprises.fr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIREN is not issued, contact INSEE. For URSSAF, ensure the K-bis is provided. If delays, follow up with the formalities portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Deposit Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in France (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale, or online banks)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name. Deposit the subscribed capital (at least 50% of cash contributions) into a blocked account. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de blocage) to be used in the RCS filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses, provide additional due diligence documents. If capital deposit is delayed, the RCS filing will be postponed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) – Customs and Excise Authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'entrepositaire agréé (Bonded Warehouse License) and Licence de débitant de boissons (if retail, but for wholesale bonded trade, the entrepositaire agréé status is required)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique (via DREAL – Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Déclaration) under the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) regime, typically under Rubrique 1510 (warehousing of flammable liquids) or 1530 (warehouses), depending on volume. Full EIA not required for bonded warehouses unless large-scale storage of hazardous substances.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with French environmental code: wastewater discharge limits per arrêté ministériel (e.g., pH 5.5-8.5, COD < 125 mg/L, BOD5 < 25 mg/L), VOC emissions per Directive 2010/75/EU (if solvent storage), and waste handling per waste management plan (plan de gestion des déchets).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire brigade (SDIS) for the warehouse, structural load inspection by a certified engineer (bureau de contrôle), and occupational health clearance from the CARSAT (regional health insurance fund) for workplace safety compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Relance; portal: impots.gouv.fr. Customs and indirect duties (including alcohol excise) administered by Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI); portal: douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Non-resident entity without permanent establishment (PE) in France: apply with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIE) using Form 1605-SD legally translated into French; DGFiP issues a French VAT number (numéro TVA intracommunautaire) and, if a PE is established, a SIREN/SIRET registration via the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE). 2) For alcoholic beverages/wine, register with DGDDI for trade and excise licences, obtaining an excise authorization (agrément d'accise). 3) For bonded operations, obtain the specific customs authorization for 'entrepôt douanier' (customs warehouse) through DGDDI. 4) Required documents include certified copy of registration certificate in country of origin, director identity, shareholding structure, proof of European or ICC transit obligations, and the scope of wine/spirits operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) is in all cases subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at the entity level on its worldwide income, subject to the territoriality limitation for permanent establishments situated abroad; only exceptional statutory transparency options (under Article 239 bis AA of the French General Tax Code) may apply within the first five fiscal years.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SAS may elect Article 239 bis AA CGI to be taxed as a société de personnes (pass-through) for eligibility-limited cases; an option for VAT grouping under Article 256 C CGI; for hybrid financing or hybrid transfer-pricing structures, anti-hybrid election and disclosure under Article 212 bis CGI and annual Form 2257-SD; treaty-based allocation of profits to foreign permanent establishment under the tax treaty network; no 'check-the-box' as in the US, but entities must file itemized elections through the income tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) — French Value Added Tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual turnover threshold for principal activity of supplying goods in mainland France; EUR 37,500 for service or other activities; no registration threshold for non-resident suppliers making any taxable supply in France (VAT obtains immediately where no French fixed establishment exists).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing reform: all B2B invoices must be issued through certified dematerialization platforms (PDP) or the French Public Invoicing Portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF) with a phased roll-out from September 2026 for large enterprises; structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII) and API submission of transactional data to DGFiP for e-reporting; real-time fiscal clearance is not applicable; for cross-border supplies, e-reporting to DGFiP is used for control; alcohol and spirits inside bond must also satisfy DGDDI electronic excise movement reports (Electronic Administrative Documents, e-AD) and customs export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the European Union qualify for the 0% VAT rate (exemption with the right to deduction) provided the goods physically leave the EU customs territory through a customs export declaration and documentary evidence of departure is held; intra-EU dispatches to a taxable customer registered for VAT also qualify for 0% subject to presentation of a valid European VAT number and recapitulative statements; wines and spirits transferred from customs warehouse (bonded warehouse) to a third country are zero-rated upon final release into export; offshore services ancillary to exported goods (freight, customs clearance, physical inspection) may also be zero-rated if directly linked to the export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation) — Single Administrative Document (SAD/DAU) accepted by DGDDI
Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR, or air waybill, together with warehouse removal certificate or transit document proving physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (for non-EU settlement) or other FX/bank confirmation of payment received in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Retrospective VAT reassessment is triggered when zero-rating is unsupported by complete export documentation; penalties under Article 1728 CGI: 40% for bad-faith failure and 80% for conscious fraud, plus late payment interest at 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI); criminal penalty exposure under Articles 412-1 and 414-1 of the French Customs Code for fraudulent export claims of up to double the evaded duties and confiscation; the tax authority’s right of reassessment is extended from the standard three-year period to six years where the export activity is hidden or fraudulent (LPF Article L186).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France and European Central Bank (ECB)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under a fully convertible currency regime for both current and capital accounts. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are unrestricted for EU-compliant entities, subject only to CRS/FATCA reporting, beneficial ownership disclosure under the French Monetary and Financial Code, and AML/KYC verification. No capital controls or profit remittance restrictions apply to properly structured French SAS entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds required under French or EU law. Exporters must submit customs declarations and report foreign exchange transactions to the Banque de France via the Système Economique de Déclaration (SED) within 30 days. Conversion to euros occurs at prevailing market rates with no forced ratios or surrender timelines.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility; French regulations impose strict licensing requirements under MiCA and the French Banking Law, prohibiting or restricting offshore electronic money institutions for cross-border activities without local partnerships and full AML compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is not strictly mandated; remote onboarding with video KYC, biometric verification, passport, and proof of address is permitted under updated French banking regulations, though enhanced due diligence applies for high-risk or bonded trade entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned jurisdiction, PEP status, or adverse media screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of funds/wealth documentation, legal entity ownership chart, independent audit reports, and beneficial ownership declarations

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or corporate registry discrepancies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declarations under the French Anti-Money Laundering Act, corporate registry extracts, and certified ownership structure

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires matching bank references, tax identification numbers, proof of equity contribution, and alignment with ECB TARGET2 settlement. French correspondent banking ensures euro-denominated compliance and regulatory reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements cleared through SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) under UCP 600. Bonded warehouse accounts must link to French customs authorizations; payments routed via approved rails to satisfy sanctions screening and avoid delays in spirits/wine settlements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) via the guichet unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts approved within six months after financial year-end; filed within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction may impose a daily penalty; failure to file may result in a EUR 1,500 fine, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat offences, and potential administrative removal after formal notice under applicable registry procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and financial schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company; electronic filing deadline may be extended under the applicable tax calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally applies at 0.20% per month, plus a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% or 80% in specified circumstances; tax assessment and audit exposure may also arise

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of shareholder and management decisions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; no routine filing authority unless a resolution requires registration or publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end for approval of annual accounts and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Management liability, shareholder claims, and potential court-ordered compliance; no automatic annual filing fee or standalone annual return applies to an SAS

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 average employees. Mandatory appointment may also arise from control, controlled-company, or group-formation rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority regulations (Plan comptable général); IFRS may be used for consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require a standalone annual UBO confirmation. Beneficial-owner information must be filed with the competent registry at incorporation and updated promptly after any change in ownership, control, or identifying information. Share transfers must be recorded in the share-transfer register and reflected in the register of shareholders; UBO changes must be reported through the applicable formal filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and share transfers
Register of decisions of shareholders and sole shareholder, where applicable
Register of decisions of the president and other corporate bodies
Minutes and attendance records for collective decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,500 annually for a registered-office or domiciliation provider; France generally does not require a separate resident registered agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 2,000-8,000 for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; larger, regulated, or group entities may incur materially higher fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first €38,120 of taxable profit for qualifying small enterprises (SME) with turnover not exceeding €7.5 million; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible qualifying R&D expenditure; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of defined innovation costs; participation exemption on qualifying long-term equity gains; territoriality rules for financing income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Déclaration de résultat) together with annexed schedules 2050 to 2059; filed electronically via the fiscal online portal impots.gouv.fr (Professionnel / EDI mode); mandatory electronic filing for all companies subject to corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional corporate income tax instalments are due quarterly on the 15th of March, June, September and December with a final balance settlement at filing date.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the annual return must be filed by the second business day following 1 May; for a fiscal year ending on any other date, the return is due within the earlier of either 30 days following the end of the fiscal year or, for certain taxpayers, the general deadline applicable to the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit or loss after re-integration of non-deductible expenses (e.g. excessive interest or director's fees) and after relief for prior-year losses; for non-residents, restricted to French-source profit attributable to the French permanent establishment (PE).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income attributable to the French PE; file the PE identification part of the form and complete the separate branch annexure; do not include foreign-source income unless treaty/protection rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Extrastatutory deductions (déductions extra-comptables) and re-integratory amounts (réintégrations), including exempt participation-exemption gains, non-deductible fines, and transfer-pricing add-backs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align French GAAP with tax basis in the PE; maintain supporting transfer pricing documentation in French tax files for the PE's related-party transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carry-forward schedule: amount of prior-year deficit applied this year and the remaining deficit to be carried forward (annual offset limited to €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit in excess of €1,000,000).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred by the French PE may be offset against future French PE profits; foreign losses cannot be carried into France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and income statement fields including fixed asset movements, depreciation/amortisation, capital gains, and provisions; required for verification of the profit reported by the SAS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide an audited or certified branch financial statement drawn under French accounting principles; reconcile the balance sheet to the French filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits applied against corporate income tax, notably CIR, family tax credit, international tax credit and any minimum tax mechanism (contribution of social solidarity).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits only on French-source qualifying expenditure; attach all required substantiation from the French PE; treaty foreign-tax credit claims require TRC and evidence of actual taxation abroad.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% surcharge plus 0.4% per month or part-month after formal demand; late payment: default interest at 0.2% per month and 5%/10% surcharge if not paid within prescribed terms; deliberate concealment triggers 40% or 80% penalty; penalties compound and are published in certain serious cases; suspension of management can be ordered.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for dividends paid by a French corporation to a non-resident corporate shareholder; no withholding tax required where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies (10%+ direct holding for 2 years) or under most French DTAs where the recipient is the beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA or Directive relief, the non-resident recipient must provide the French paying entity with a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its tax authorities, a completed Form 5000 or 5001 where applicable, and evidence of 2-year holding period; the paying entity applies the reduced rate when the certificate is in hand before the payment date; if excess tax was withheld, a refund claim may be submitted within the statutory limitation period using form 3508-SD.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties/licences paid to non-resident legal entities: domestic withholding at 33.33% (plus possible guaranteed tax levies); under DTAs rates are generally 0% or 5%–10% depending on type of intellectual property; interest on ordinary bank loans to non-resident lenders: 0% domestic withholding, and general treaty reductions to 0%; certain bond interest paid to non-residents remains subject to a 12.8% domestic levy; payments to Non-Cooperative Tax Jurisdictions (ETNC) attract a 75% withholding tax unless bona fide and substance conditions are proven.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400 million (annual turnover or gross total assets of the French entity or the group it controls/belongs to) triggers mandatory Local File and Master File obligations; OECD Country-by-Country Report is required for groups whose consolidated annual revenue is €750 million or more.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although France does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, genuine economic substance is a core requirement for treaty benefits, for exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, and for avoiding the principal-purpose test under the MLI. A French SAS engaged in bonded wholesale wine and spirit trading must maintain real substance: local decision-making, qualified staff, stock custody records, warehouse licences, customs bonds and independent books. Shielding activity behind a shell French entity without local management will expose it to anti-abuse challenges under Art. L.64 LPF and to taxation of its passive income under CFC rules (Art. 209 B).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable profit, omission of sales derived from bonded warehouse deliveries, use of fictitious invoices, movement of spirits without excise records, or false VAT and excise duty declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty up to 80% of the concealed amounts plus monthly default interest; criminal conviction under Art. 1741 of the French General Tax Code carries a fine of up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (raised to €1,000,000 and 7 years when aggravated by laundering); publication of the sanction may be ordered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS President or effective director may be jointly liable for the corporate tax debts under Art. L.266 LPF; criminal liability extends to the personal estate, civil restitution, temporary or permanent travel ban, inability to manage commercial companies, and prison sentence; a criminal conviction can trigger asset seizure and asset freezing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing related foreign distributors below arm's-length commodity prices for wine or spirits, paying excessive royalties to an offshore IP owner, placing central procurement functions in a low-tax country without actual substance, or failure to file TP documentation once the threshold is met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to arm's-length level, default interest at 0.2% per month, 40% penalty for serious mispricing under Art. 1735 CGI; Country-by-Country Report non-filing penalties may reach €100,000; comparable penalties apply for missing Master File/Local File upon tax audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where deliberate mispricing is proven, directors can be held personally liable under the theory of intentional fault; in case of insolvency, the commercial court can impose a financial contribution; criminal liability for misuse of corporate assets (abus de biens sociaux) carries up to €375,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment; directors can be barred from departing the territory during an investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law / Shell Company Scheme
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French SAS with no genuine warehouse operations, staff, stock or decisions, used purely to channel invoices for Bordeaux wines and spirits, claim VAT/customs credits, or obtain DTA benefits through a treaty-shopping vehicle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the abuse-of-law doctrine (Art. L.64 LPF): penalty of 80% (or 100% when abuse is supported by fictitious acts or sham clauses), recapture of excise/customs duty entitlements, nullification of VAT credits, and denial of treaty benefits under the principal-purpose test; suspension of the business licence for bonded trade may be ordered by the customs administration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally use a sham entity are criminally liable for tax fraud and may receive fines, imprisonment, prohibition from holding office, travel ban and seizure of personal property; the corporate veil is pierced and the court may impose joint and several liability for unpaid taxes, penalties and customs duties of the entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform adequate KYC/AML controls on bonded warehouse customers, moving proceeds derived from counterfeit-critique sales or excise duty evasion, dealing with sanctioned entities or jurisdictions in wine/spirit export transactions, and falsifying warehouse movement records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French Criminal Code Art. 421-1 and related money-laundering provisions impose imprisonment up to 10 years and fines up to €750,000 for intentional laundering; customs penalties for false or non-existent customs declarations include goods confiscation, fines of one to three times the value of the goods, and withdrawal of the authorised bonded warehouse licence; banking and AML damages are additional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS president and effective management face criminal prosecution where substantive AML controls were knowingly omitted; the court may issue a travel ban, freezing orders, disqualification from commercial activity, and civil liability to compensate authorities and aggrieved parties; piercing the corporate veil is available when the legal entity is used as an instrument of fraud.
